class.name: FoliagePainter3D
class.brief_description: Paints one or more kinds of vegetation onto other meshes with a brush, in the editor.
class.description: [FoliagePainter3D] holds a list of [member layers] (vegetation types, each a [FoliageLayer]) and renders each one through its own internal [MultiMeshInstance3D]. It is the counterpart to [FoliageSpawner3D]'s procedural box-volume scattering: instead of filling a volume automatically, instances are painted, erased, or placed/removed one at a time directly onto the actual surface geometry of any [MeshInstance3D] in the scene, using the brush tool that appears in the 3D viewport's toolbar while a [FoliagePainter3D] is selected. Add at least one [FoliageLayer] to [member layers] (each with a [member FoliageLayer.mesh] assigned) before using the brush. The brush toolbar lets you choose which layers it paints with at once, its radius and density, and one of four modes: - [b]Paint[/b]: click or drag over a mesh surface to scatter instances of the active layers within the brush, with random scale, rotation, and normal deviation controlled per layer (see [member FoliageLayer.min_scale], [member FoliageLayer.random_rotation], [member FoliageLayer.align_to_normal_amount], and [member FoliageLayer.random_tilt_degrees]). - [b]Erase[/b]: click or drag to remove instances of the active layers found within the brush. - [b]Place Single[/b]: click to insert exactly one instance at the exact clicked point. - [b]Remove Single[/b]: click to delete the single closest instance to the clicked point. Painting only looks at [MeshInstance3D] geometry; no physics bodies or collision shapes are required on the painted-on meshes. Each layer's visible distance can be configured independently through [member FoliageLayer.visibility_range_begin] and related properties, so nearby dense foliage (e.g. grass) can be culled at a much shorter distance than larger background vegetation. While instances are usually added and removed through the brush, [method insert_instance], [method remove_instance], and [method add_instance] are also available for scripted or procedural editing of a layer's [MultiMesh].

method.name: add_instance
method.description: Appends a new instance with the given [param transform] to the layer at [param layer_index], and returns its index. Equivalent to calling [method insert_instance] with an index equal to [method get_layer_instance_count].

method.name: get_layer
method.description: Returns the [FoliageLayer] at [param layer_index] in [member layers].

method.name: get_layer_count
method.description: Returns the number of layers in [member layers].

method.name: get_layer_instance_count
method.description: Returns the number of instances currently painted for the layer at [param layer_index].

method.name: get_layer_instance_transform
method.description: Returns the local-space transform of instance [param index] of the layer at [param layer_index].

method.name: insert_instance
method.description: Inserts a new instance with the given local-space [param transform] at [param index] in the layer at [param layer_index], shifting any existing instances at or after [param index] up by one. [param index] is clamped to the current instance count, so passing the current count appends the instance.

method.name: remove_instance
method.description: Removes instance [param index] from the layer at [param layer_index], shifting any subsequent instances down by one.

members.member: The vegetation types this node can paint. Each entry is a [FoliageLayer] with its own [Mesh], randomization settings, brush density/spacing, and visibility range. Add and configure entries from the Inspector, then select this node to paint with the brush tool in the 3D viewport.
